_note: Only 'option', 'nbSim_values', 'nSamples', 'output_dir' are read by run_study. All '_*' keys are ignored — use them as comments. To switch option type, replace the 'option' block below with one of the examples at the bottom of this file.
_note_nbSim: nbSim_values drives the convergence sweep — each value is one data point on the graphs. nbSim inside 'option' is ignored.
_note_nSamples: nSamples controls how many paths are collected for the terminal distribution and antithetic scatter plots (not the convergence sweep).
_note_notebook: After running: open demo/analysis.ipynb in Jupyter, update S0/K/r/sigma/T/option_label at the top to match your option, then Run All.

_examples._ex1_description: 1D European call — plain vanilla, 1 step is exact for GBM (no discretization bias). All 5 variance reduction methods apply.
_examples._ex2_description: Bermudan call — quarterly exercise dates, more steps needed for the regression. Only 'none' and 'qmc' variance reduction are available for Bermudan.
_examples._ex3_description: 2D basket call — two correlated assets, equal weights. staticcv and qmc_cv use the geometric basket closed form as control variate (it has an exact price).
_examples._ex4_description: 3D basket call — three assets, unequal weights and different volatilities. Shows how the variance reduction scales to higher dimensions.
_examples._ex5_description: High-vol OTM European call — most paths expire worthless, variance is high. Good to compare antithetic vs QMC on a hard distribution.
